operations.specification: Implements the user registration (join) endpoint for the Todo List Application. It handles new user sign-ups by accepting a unique email and password, then creates a new user account in the todo_user table. The Prisma model defines unique email enforcement and secure password hash storage. The endpoint exclusively targets the todo_user table, ensuring every registration results in a unique user row with only email (unique) and password_hash fields, plus standard created_at and updated_at timestamps. The operation issues a JWT token for session management aligned with business rules for isolated access to todos. The endpoint is strictly audited for account uniqueness, data privacy, and minimum permissions (no admin/social/profile creation).
operations.description:
This endpoint supports account registration for new users in the Todo List Application by creating a new row in the todo_user table. 

Requests must provide a valid, unique email address (see the 'email' field in the schema: 'Unique email address for authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all users and adhere to standard email formatting.') and a raw password for hashing and storage in the 'password_hash' field ('Secure hash of the user's password. Stored using strong cryptographic practices. Never stores raw passwords.').

On successful registration, the new user's record is created with associated timestamps: 'created_at' as the instant of creation, 'updated_at' matching 'created_at', and a null 'deleted_at' field indicating it is active. All session management, business rule enforcement, and unique account creation logic are enforced here as described in the requirements document.

The endpoint does not integrate social login, phone verification, or additional roles/profiles. Only direct, per-user sign-up is supported.

If an email already exists, the endpoint returns a business-level registration error (no technical leakage of user existence), enforcing the uniqueness constraint described in the Prisma schema.

This endpoint is the initial step for account creation; users must subsequently authenticate via login with issued credentials and may request token refresh when needed.
operations.summary: Register a new user in todo_user table, enforcing email uniqueness and strong password policies.

requestBody.description: Registration data with user email and password.

responseBody.description: Registration response with issued authorization token.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implements user login for the Todo List Application using email and password credentials. Authenticates a user by verifying the credentials against the todo_user table, which contains the email field (unique constraint) and the securely hashed password_hash field. The endpoint creates a JWT session and issues tokens on successful authentication. Session invalidation and token lifetimes are managed per the requirements, including expiration after 30 days of inactivity. The endpoint does not extend permission to access or alter any todos except those owned by the authenticated user, as per core business requirements.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables registered users to authenticate by submitting their email ('email' field, unique, mandatory in todo_user schema) and raw password (checked against the 'password_hash' field using secure verification). 

Upon successful verification, the system issues a JWT token as described in the requirements, including userId claims and session timing based on 'created_at'/'updated_at' timestamps. Only users with active, non-deleted accounts ('deleted_at' must be null) may successfully log in.

Failed login attempts for invalid credentials never disclose account existence or technical errors. Errors are presented as uniform authentication failures matching security guidelines. 

On successful authentication, the session follows strict rules: session expiration after 30 days, log out/invalidation support, and user data isolation as required by the business processes and permission matrix documented.

No role elevation, admin, or additional attributes are ever exposed via this endpoint. All logic references the todo_user schema for registration, credential checking, and session management.
operations.summary: Authenticate a user from todo_user table and issue a JWT token if credentials are valid.

requestBody.description: User login credentials: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication response including authorization JWT and session details.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implements token refresh for authenticated users of the Todo List Application, based on an existing valid refresh token. This operation looks up the associated user from the todo_user table, validates session timing via session storage (in unmodeled session table or stateless JWT), and reissues new JWT access tokens. No additional user data or permissions are granted; refresh only maintains the validity of an existing active session. Business enforcement is based on session timing, 'created_at', and 'updated_at' in todo_user.
operations.description:
This endpoint refreshes the JWT authorization token for an authenticated user whose current session remains valid. It checks the refresh token's association in the session system (either via sessions table or token content referencing the todo_user primary key).

The system validates session timing constraints (inactivity window, as enforced by the 'created_at' and 'updated_at' fields of the todo_user schema and session lifetime rules from requirements). On success, a new JWT and refresh token are issued, not exposing underlying credential or user details.

This endpoint does not permit re-activation of deleted ('deleted_at' not null) or invalid/expired user accounts. Uniform error responses are given for expired or invalid tokens.

Token refresh operations must precede any attempts to access Todo data if the original session is expired.

No account creation, update, or role adjustment occurs here. Solely refreshes authorization on existing valid sessions per business and schema rules.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT authorization token for an authenticated todo_user session.

requestBody.description: Refresh token submission for session renewal.

responseBody.description: New JWT authorization token for user session continuation.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of user accounts from the todo_user table. It enables advanced searching and sorting based on user email, and can be used for administrative review of current and soft-deleted users. The search leverages the unique email field and supports filtering by creation, update, and deletion timestamp fields as defined in the schema. Results comply with user privacy and isolation mandates as described in the schema documentation.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of user accounts within the Todo List Application.

This endpoint allows administrators to perform advanced queries for users based on unique email, soft deletion status, and various timestamp fields such as account creation and update times. All filtering logic closely follows the field definitions in the todo_user schema, ensuring operations remain consistent with data privacy and security requirements.

A key aspect of this operation is respect for user isolation and right-to-be-forgotten compliance. Administrators can filter for accounts flagged as soft-deleted via the deleted_at field. When reviewing results, sensitive password hashes and internal identifiers are not exposed in the default summary view. Related business rules and roles are enforced strictly at the query and result-response level for maximum data security.

Pagination is provided to efficiently support large user bases and performance best practices. The operation is only available to users with user-level access; no higher-privileged roles are defined in schema.
operations.summary: Paginated search for todo_user accounts with advanced filters and privacy compliance.

requestBody.description: Request body containing email filters, timestamp ranges, sort options, soft deletion filter, and pagination parameters for user search.

responseBody.description: A paginated summary list of users matching provided filters and user access rules.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the full detailed record of a single user from the todo_user table, identified by UUID primary key. The endpoint directly reflects all currently active and soft-deleted (deleted_at non-null) users for thorough administrative insight. No other unique code or composite key is available, so userId—corresponding to the id field in the schema—is used as the identifier. The operation exposes all major user fields except password hashes, including email, creation/update timestamps, and deletion status. All business rules on privacy, security, and user isolation are strictly applied as defined in the schema.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed information for a single user account in the Todo List Application using the unique user identifier (UUID).

The endpoint returns all critical account information including unique email, account creation time, last update time, and soft deletion timestamp (if applicable – for right-to-be-forgotten support). Access is strictly scoped to users with 'user' role; no admin-level access is available per schema. Password hash data is never exposed in responses.

This operation helps users audit their individual account, review historical modifications, and enforce system-wide privacy and security policies. Only fields explicitly defined in the schema are presented, and ownership/permissions are strongly enforced according to application rules. Querying a user who is soft-deleted returns their record including the deleted_at value; permanently erased users are not returned, resulting in a not found error.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed attributes of a single todo_user account for user review.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Primary key UUID of the user to retrieve. Must match the id field in the todo_user schema.

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested user account, matching all schema definitions for todo_user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing user account in the Todo List Application, using the todo_user table as its data source. The operation allows modifications to core account properties such as email and password_hash. It enforces uniqueness on the email address and validates inputs according to the Prisma schema's constraints for email format and password security. The update timestamp is automatically set. The userId in the path identifies the target user record by UUID primary key.
operations.summary: Update a user's account information (todo_user table)
operations.description:
Update an existing user account's information, such as their email address or password hash.

This operation allows the modifying of the account's core details: the unique email and password_hash. Email changes are validated for format and uniqueness, ensuring there are no duplicates across all user accounts. Password hashes must use secure cryptographic practices according to policy, and raw passwords are never accepted. The updated_at field is automatically set to the current timestamp on each modification.

The operation references the todo_user table, leveraging the field-level constraints as documented in the schema. The operation only permits authenticated users or administrators to modify user data, ensuring account isolation and privacy compliance. Invalid email formats, duplicated emails, or insecure passwords will result in validation errors, and no changes will be made unless all rules are satisfied.

Security: Proper authorization is required—either the user updating their own account or an administrator with appropriate privileges. Attempts to update non-existent or soft-deleted accounts are rejected with a clear error response. Related operations include account deletion (DELETE /users/{userId}).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account to be updated (primary key of todo_user).

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the user account (email, password_hash); must comply with uniqueness and security constraints.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a user account from the todo_user table using the provided userId path parameter (the UUID primary key). Instead of hard deletion, this operation sets the deleted_at field to the current timestamp, marking the account as soft-deleted in accordance with compliance policies (GDPR, right-to-be-forgotten). Only users themselves or authorized administrators may perform this operation. Deleted accounts cannot be authenticated or accessed, supporting strict data privacy and security.
operations.summary: Soft-delete (flag as deleted) a user account (todo_user table)
operations.description:
Mark a user account as deleted by updating the deleted_at timestamp (soft delete), following data retention and privacy compliance requirements.

This operation flags the target user account as deleted without actually removing the record from the database, following GDPR and right-to-be-forgotten standards where applicable. The deleted_at field is set to the current timestamp, and the user will no longer be able to log in or access any system functionality.

Affected records remain in the database for audit and compliance, supporting retention policies. Accessing or operating on soft-deleted accounts results in rejection and clear error messaging. Related operations include user update (PUT /users/{userId}). Only the user themselves or administrators acting in compliance with security protocols can perform this operation. Irreversible deletion (physical removal) must be handled by a separate, privileged process if needed.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account to be deleted (primary key of todo_user).

responseBody.description: Soft-deleted user account after marking deleted_at.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated and filtered list of authentication sessions for a specific user from the todo_user_sessions table in the database. Each session record represents a single authenticated login for the user as identified by their userId. This endpoint is intended for audit, personal user history, or cross-device management, allowing the user to trace all of their login sessions for transparency and security.

The response includes essential details for each session, including originating IP address, session creation and expiration timestamps, connection URLs, and associated metadata for account audit. The search criteria provided in the request body allow advanced filtering of sessions based on creation times, status, or attributes such as IP. Related operations include viewing single-session details or searching across all users (admin API only).

This operation is strictly read-only and is exposed to authenticated users for visibility and cross-device account management. The endpoint requires the userId (UUID) as the path parameter and only allows access to the currently authenticated user's sessions.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of your own authentication sessions by userId in the path. This is designed for ordinary users ("user" role) to view their own session history for cross-device management, logout, or security monitoring.

The response provides comprehensive session activity records, including connection context, IP address, and login/referrer URLs, so that users can review past account access and notice suspicious activity. Search and filtering is performed via criteria in the request body, allowing filtering by creation date, active/expired status, or device/session attributes. Pagination and sorting are also supported for efficiency.

Security ensures a user may only view their own sessions (the userId must match the authenticated user's id). All results are filtered accordingly, and there is never visibility into other users' sessions.
operations.summary: Search and paginate your own authentication sessions (todo_user_sessions table).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account (must be the currently authenticated user).

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for todo_user_sessions records of the user.

responseBody.description: Paginated and filtered list of session summaries for the requested user account.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific authentication session belonging to a user from the todo_user_sessions table, for audit or cross-device management purposes. It allows an authenticated user to view full context on a particular login, including all captured metadata such as origin IP, href, referrer, start and expiration times.

The userId and sessionId must both be provided as UUID path parameters to uniquely identify the session within the context of the user account. Security checks ensure the currently authenticated user matches the userId parameter, so users can only view their own session data. The operation is strictly read-only, providing full details but never exposing modification or removal operations. Related endpoints allow listing all sessions for a user or deleting sessions (if implemented by business rules).

This API endpoint is exposed to authenticated users for audit, history, or account management purposes.
operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a specific authentication session belonging to the requesting user, using both the userId and sessionId passed as path parameters.

The response contains all available session metadata, including time of login, connection origin, referrer, and expiration. This operation allows users to audit their own account usage and spot unauthorized logins or forgotten sessions on other devices.

Security is provided by restricting this endpoint to authenticated users, and all responses are filtered so that only the owner's session details can be accessed. UserId must match the authenticated identity.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about your own authentication session (todo_user_sessions table).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account (must be the currently authenticated user).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target authentication session for the user.

responseBody.description: Detailed session record and connection/audit context for the queried session.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Retrieves a paginated and filtered list of todo_todos records. This operation supports complex searching and list pagination to allow users to view their own todos with fine-grained filtering, search, and sorting. It is based on the todo_todos table, enforcing strict per-user data isolation at both database and API levels. Query parameters include filtering by completion status or date ranges, searching by title and/or description, and paginating results. Only the authenticated user's todos are returned; no cross-user access is possible.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todo tasks belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation allows a user to search and filter their personal todo items using a set of advanced query parameters, such as keyword matching on the todo title and filtering by completion status or creation date range. The endpoint enforces that only the owning user's data is accessible, ensuring privacy and data isolation as required by the underlying Prisma schema and business requirements.

Supports pagination and sorting by relevant fields (title, created_at, completed) to optimize list display in client applications. Underlying security design guarantees that all filters are scoped to the authenticated user's record set. Related endpoints include creation (POST /todos), detail retrieval (GET /todos/{todoId}), updating (PUT /todos/{todoId}), completion toggling, and permanent erasure (DELETE /todos/{todoId}). Soft deletion is not supported—deletions are always permanent per the schema.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, user-scoped list of todos from todo_todos.

requestBody.description: Filter and pagination parameters for searching the todos list. Only fields relevant to the authenticated user's own todos are supported.

responseBody.description: Paginated response containing summaries of matching todo tasks for the authenticated user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieves a single todo_todos record by unique todoId for detailed viewing. This operation provides full detail of a todo task, including all fields defined in the todo_todos table: title, optional description, completion state, and associated timestamps. The endpoint ensures only the owner user can access the todo with the given ID, maintaining strict data isolation and privacy guarantees. The todoId parameter maps to the UUID primary key of the todo_todos table, and authorization is enforced such that users may never access another user's todo. The response body provides the complete ITodoTodo DTO for the requested record.
operations.description:
Retrieve all details of a specific todo task, owned by the authenticated user.

This operation lets a user access complete information for a single todo item using its UUID. It returns the full detail as per the todo_todos schema including title, description, completion state, and creation/update/completion timestamps. Business rules ensure that only the owning user is allowed access, preventing data leaks or cross-user data exposure.

Appropriate errors are returned if the todo does not exist or if the user lacks access. Related operations include list retrieval (PATCH /todos), creation, modification, and permanent deletion. There is no soft-delete mechanism—deleted todos are removed entirely per privacy policy.
operations.summary: Retrieve detail of a specific todo by todo_todos primary key.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the todo_todos record to retrieve. Must belong to the requesting user.

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the specified todo task, if found and owned by the requesting user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new personal todo item for the authenticated user. It utilizes the todo_todos table, which represents the core business entity for each task. Each todo contains a required short title (max 255 characters, unique per user), an optional description (up to 1000 characters), and is automatically linked to the creating user's account. By default, the completed status is false, and the relevant timestamps (created_at/updated_at) are managed by the system. User ownership and per-user uniqueness of title are strictly enforced at the database and business logic levels. The todo is only visible to its owner, and all fields are validated for length and presence on create. No collaboration, sharing, or non-personal features exist; all creation operations are fully private, minimalist, and strictly consistent with the business requirements and schema.
operations.description:
Create a new todo task for the authenticated user in the personal todo list.

This operation allows the currently logged-in user to add a new todo item, specifying a required title and an optional description. The system enforces input validation for field presence (title), maximum allowed lengths (255 for title, 1000 for description), and ensures the title is not empty or whitespace-only. Titles are unique for each user, preventing duplicate creation within one account. The completed status is set to false by default; timestamps are managed automatically.

Security is strictly enforced—the user must be authenticated, and the todo is always assigned to the user's own account. Unauthorized or unauthenticated creation attempts are denied. There is no possibility for sharing or collaborative creation; all todos are strictly single-user and private.

If required fields are missing, validation fails, or constraints are violated (such as title non-uniqueness per user), the operation returns clear, actionable error messages. Only fields specified by requirements and schema are accepted; extraneous input is rejected. No extra metadata is stored or allowed.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item (todo_todos table) for the current user.

requestBody.description: Details for the todo to create, including title (required, max 255) and optional description (max 1000). Must not be empty or whitespace-only.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item, including all fields (id, title, description, completion, timestamps, etc).

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo in the todo_todos table for the authenticated user. Only the owner of the todo may perform this operation. Updatable fields include the title (must remain unique within the user's todos, required, max 255, not blank/whitespace), the optional description (may be set, removed, or shortened, max 1000), and the completion status (boolean, toggling will update completion timestamp accordingly). Creation timestamp is immutable; updates always refresh the updated_at field. Ownership and access are strictly enforced according to business logic and schema. Unauthorized users or those attempting to update non-owned or missing todos receive forbidden/not found errors. All validation rules (max length, required, uniqueness, etc.) are applied; fields not in schema are ignored. Permanent, private, fully user-owned operation.
operations.description:
Update a todo item that belongs exclusively to the authenticated user.

This operation permits the user to change the title, description, or completion status of an existing todo item, provided they are the sole owner. The title must remain not empty, unique, and within length limits; description changes are optional and may be set, cleared, or shortened as needed (subject to constraints). Completion may be toggled freely—setting or unsetting also manages the completed_at timestamp. Attempted modifications by unauthorized users or to non-existent or non-owned todos always result in forbidden or not found errors.

Input is fully validated: title (required, non-empty, max 255, unique per user), description (optional, max 1000), completed (boolean). The creation timestamp remains fixed, while updated_at and completed_at are system-managed. This operation strictly adheres to business rules for privacy, ownership, and data integrity.

Success returns the new state of the todo; all errors are precise and actionable. No extra features, sharing, or collaborative edits are permitted—operation is minimalist by design and schema.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo item (todo_todos table) belonging to the current user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (owned by the authenticated user).

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the todo. Includes required title (max 255), optional description (max 1000), and completed status (boolean).

responseBody.description: The updated todo item reflecting all changes.

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created before it can be updated. The update operation requires a valid todoId corresponding to an existing todo belonging to the authenticated user.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific todo item from the "todo_todos" table. Each todo represents a user-owned task, uniquely identified by its primary key ID. When this DELETE endpoint is invoked, the referenced todo is completely removed from the database, with no archiving or soft deletion. This complies with the documented business requirement that deletion must be permanent, respecting privacy and data lifecycle enforcement at the persistence layer. The operation requires the unique todo ID as a path parameter and ensures that only the owner or an authorized actor can perform deletion.
operations.description:
Delete a specific todo item associated with the currently authenticated user. The operation requires the unique identifier of the target todo task as a path parameter. Once invoked, the operation removes the todo task from persistent storage permanently.

Security enforcement ensures that only the owner of the todo (identified by 'todo_user_id') or an authorized administrative actor can delete the resource. No soft delete or archiving is performed; deletion is permanent, as required by strict privacy rules and business policy in the Prisma schema. All associated timestamps and metadata are lost upon deletion.

Error scenarios include: trying to delete a non-existent or already-deleted task (results in 404), attempting to delete a todo that does not belong to the current user (results in 403), or providing an invalid or non-UUID ID (results in 400). Related operations include creation, listing, updating, and toggling the completion state of todos. This endpoint plays a critical role in upholding user control over their own data lifecycle, in compliance with privacy regulations.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item from the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the todo item to be deleted.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created before it can be deleted; this operation ensures the todo item exists prior to deletion.

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: An authenticated individual who can manage their own todo items via the API. Users can create, read, update, complete, and delete their personal todo tasks, but cannot access or modify tasks of others.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoUser.IJoin.description:
Registration DTO for new users of the Todo List Application, engineered for maximum privacy, GDPR compliance, and strict account isolation.

Used as the request body for the user registration endpoint. Accepts only a unique email and plaintext password alongside session context metadata required for audit and regulatory enforcement.

Upon validation (unique email and password policies), results in the creation of a new todo_user table row. No profile, roles, username, or additional identity fields are accepted, guaranteeing that no non-essential metadata is collected during registration — only what is required for account creation and privacy-compliant auditing is accepted.

The backend hashes passwords on receipt (no pre-hashed passwords are accepted or stored), and session context is only captured for legal audit, user activity tracking, and security monitoring per requirements.

No social login, profile customization, extended field set, or multi-user/join/group logic exists in this DTO. Designed for the most minimal user footprint possible, as required by privacy policy, security standards, and GDPR.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) must be provided for audit trails and security event reconstruction. These fields are not persisted to the user record but auditable at the registration boundary.

email.description: User email for authentication and account recovery. Must be unique among all users. Validated for RFC 5322 compliance as per schema.

password.description: Raw user password for account registration (minimum 8 characters recommended). The backend hashes this value before storing in password_hash column. Never accept pre-hashed values from the client.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (optional). If not supplied, the server may extract from request metadata.

href.description: Current page URL (at the time of sign-up). Used for audit trails and risk analysis. Must be supplied by the client.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (the URL from which the sign-up was initiated). Used for session audit, marketing attribution, and risk analysis. Must be supplied by the client; can be empty string for direct navigation.

ITodoUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication/Authorization response for successful join or login of a Todo List Application user.

Contains the unique user id, an issued JWT (and refresh token if appropriate), and essential details for establishing an authenticated session in the client. May be reused for join, login, and token refresh endpoints.

Never exposes password hash or sensitive authentication details. Only exposes what is required for authenticated session setup.

id.description: Primary key of the user (todo_user.id). Unique identifier for the authenticated user.

email.description:
Unique email address for authentication and account recovery.

This email must be globally unique across all user accounts, following standard email formatting. Used for login, system notifications, and password recovery flows.

Validation: Must match RFC 5322 email format. Uniqueness enforced at the database level. Update operations must also respect uniqueness constraint.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was first created.

Immutable once set. Used for account age calculations, auditing, and ordering by registration date.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to this user record. Automatically updated on modifications to email, password, or deletion status. Useful for determining recent account activity.

oneOf.description: Timestamp marking when the account was soft-deleted (for compliance with GDPR, right-to-be-forgotten, or admin actions). Non-null indicates the account is no longer active or able to log in.
Null value indicates account is still active and not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Indicates whether this account is soft-deleted. If non-null, contains the deletion timestamp. Otherwise, the account is active.

ITodoUser.ILogin.description:
Login DTO for authenticating users in the Todo List Application.

Submitted as request body to the login endpoint. Consists of the user's email address and raw password required for credential verification. Session context fields are required per system login requirements: 'href' (URL of login request) and 'referrer' (previous page URL). 'ip' is optional and can be provided for SSR logging or left null for automatic server extraction.

Only valid if targeting a real, undeleted todo_user record.

email.description:
Email address of the user attempting authentication. Must match the unique email field in the todo_user table. Required.

Validated against standard RFC 5322 email format. Serves as the principal identifier for user login and must already exist in the todo_user table for successful login. Not case-sensitive.

password.description: Raw user password for credential verification. Used to check against the password_hash in the todo_user table according to strong cryptographic rules. Never stored or logged in plaintext. Handled securely during verification.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address from which this login attempt originated. If omitted or null, extracted server-side.
Unset/null if not provided by the client; extracted from the request automatically.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session audit and traceability. Optional. If not provided, the backend extracts it from the connection context.

Used for security analysis and session logging; can be null when unavailable. IPv4 or IPv6 accepted.

href.description: The full URL (href) at which the login request was initiated. MANDATORY for security tracing and session context. Must match the page URL on the client.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page) for this login request. MANDATORY session context field.

Allows origin auditing and helps detect suspicious authentication patterns. Required by the session system.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description:
DTO for submitting a refresh token to obtain renewed authentication for the Todo List Application.

Sent as request body to the refresh endpoint when a user needs to prolong their session. Contains only the refresh token issued previously. No user-identifying information is accepted—session lookup is handled automatically.

Supports session continuity and enforces single-user isolation with no role/permission escalation.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token for session renewal. Uniquely identifies an authenticated session—must match a valid, active todo_user_sessions record.

Trusted only if issued by the system in a previous authenticated flow. Sensitive to expiration and session revocation policies.

id.description: Primary key UUID uniquely identifying this user. Serves as the canonical identity for login, relationship mapping, and all account operations. Generated automatically and never reused. Required for all references and update operations.

email.description:
Unique email address for authentication and account recovery.

This email must be globally unique across all user accounts, following standard email formatting. Used for login, system notifications, and password recovery flows.

Validation: Must match RFC 5322 email format. Uniqueness enforced at the database level. Update operations must also respect uniqueness constraint.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was first created.

Immutable once set. Used for account age calculations, auditing, and ordering by registration date.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to this user record. Automatically updated on modifications to email, password, or deletion status. Useful for determining recent account activity.

oneOf.description: Timestamp marking when the account was soft-deleted (for compliance with GDPR, right-to-be-forgotten, or admin actions). Non-null indicates the account is no longer active or able to log in.
Null value indicates account is still active and not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Indicates whether this account is soft-deleted. If non-null, contains the deletion timestamp. Otherwise, the account is active.

ITodoUser.description:
A registered user account in the Todo List Application.

Users represent individuals able to log in, own todos, and manage personal lists. Each user is uniquely identified by a UUID primary key and a globally unique email. The model enforces account isolation, privacy, and right-to-be-forgotten via the deleted_at field. No password hash or authentication credential is ever exposed here.

System and security fields (password hash) are strictly server-side; only business-facing attributes are present. Timestamps support auditing and compliance. Schema aligns with the todo_user table in the database.

q.description:
A search string applied to filter user email addresses.

Allows partial or full matching against the unique email field as per database-level LIKE/ILIKE semantics. Non-empty strings perform filtering; empty or omitted uses all accounts.

email.description:
Direct filter for an exact email address match.

Overrides q search behavior for targeted retrieval. Must adhere to RFC 5322 email format and exist in the database for a match.

created_from.description: Restrict results to users created on or after this timestamp.

created_to.description: Restrict results to users created on or before this timestamp.

updated_from.description: Only include users updated on or after this timestamp.

updated_to.description: Only include users updated on or before this timestamp.

deleted.description: True to search only for soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at non-null); false to search only active accounts (deleted_at is null). Omit to include all users regardless of deletion state.

oneOf.description: Field to sort user search results by. Supported: email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Defaults to created_at if not specified.
Field to sort user search results by. Supported: email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Defaults to created_at if not specified.
Field to sort user search results by. Supported: email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Defaults to created_at if not specified.
Field to sort user search results by. Supported: email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Defaults to created_at if not specified.

sort_by.description: Field to sort user search results by. Supported: email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Defaults to created_at if not specified.

oneOf.description: Sorting order direction: asc for ascending or desc for descending.
Sorting order direction: asc for ascending or desc for descending.

sort_order.description: Sorting order direction: asc for ascending or desc for descending.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of users per page in results. Default and maximum may be set by server configuration.

ITodoUser.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching or filtering user accounts in the Todo List Application.

Supports advanced search, sort, and pagination for the todo_user entity. Provides for flexible querying by email, creation and update timestamps, soft-deletion status, and other audit fields. Used in PATCH /todo/user/users operation.

Field selection aligns with business and privacy requirements to ensure only user-accessible search fields are exposed.

ITodoUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating a user's core account information in the Todo List Application.

This DTO enables modification of the user's core details—specifically the email address and password hash—by directly updating the corresponding fields in the todo_user Prisma model. Only mutable account attributes are exposed; immutable properties such as account creation, update, and deletion timestamps and the user ID are strictly excluded, ensuring robust system integrity and traceability.

The email property must be globally unique and conform to RFC 5322 email format, supporting both authentication and account recovery. The password_hash field replaces prior authentication data and must always be provided as a secure cryptographic hash; raw passwords are never accepted per business policy.

All update operations leverage automatic timestamping for the updated_at column, supporting audit trails and compliance logging. Attempts to modify immutable or system-managed fields via this DTO will be rejected by the implementation layer. These design rules are enforced for maximum data privacy, user account isolation, and auditing compliance.

email.description:
A new email address for the user account in the todo_user table.

Must be unique across all user records and follow valid email address formatting according to RFC 5322 standards. Changing the email address triggers uniqueness and format validation; failure will reject the update. This field enables user authentication as well as password recovery workflows.

password_hash.description:
A new secure hash of the user's password, replacing the prior password_hash value in the database.

This field must be set only with a cryptographically secure password hash, never a raw password. All password updates use secure salting and hashing algorithms as per policy; the hash is never exposed in response DTOs or API results.

ITodoUserSession.IRequest.description:
Query parameters and filtering criteria for searching a user's own authentication sessions in the Todo List Application.

Provides flexible search and filtering over todo_user_sessions records, enabling filtering by creation date, session status, originating IP, and connection context. Used for paginated audit and history views, cross-device management, and security monitoring. Designed for robust search criteria without exposing implementation internals. Intended for the user to only view their own sessions; never applied to other users or admin accounts.

page.description: The pagination page number for the session search results. Used for limiting the result set to reasonable, manageable chunks.

limit.description: Maximum count of sessions to return per page. Restricts the number of session records returned, capped to prevent large payloads and performance issues. Recommended range: 1-100.

search.description: Optional search term for session metadata. Used to filter sessions based on contextual information, such as part of the IP address, referrer, or connection URL. Not intended for field-specific granular queries.

created_from.description: Filter start date for search, in ISO 8601 format. Only include sessions created at or after this timestamp. Used for time window filtering.

created_to.description: Filter end date for search, in ISO 8601 format. Only include sessions created at or before this timestamp. Used for time window filtering.

ip.description: Optional filter to restrict sessions by originating IP address. Used for investigating suspicious logins or device history.

oneOf.description: Session status filter. Used to limit result set to active, expired, or all sessions as needed for device management and audit. Only permitted values are 'all', 'active', or 'expired'.
Session status filter. Used to limit result set to active, expired, or all sessions as needed for device management and audit. Only permitted values are 'all', 'active', or 'expired'.
Session status filter. Used to limit result set to active, expired, or all sessions as needed for device management and audit. Only permitted values are 'all', 'active', or 'expired'.

status.description: Session status filter. Used to limit result set to active, expired, or all sessions as needed for device management and audit. Only permitted values are 'all', 'active', or 'expired'.

ITodoUserSession.description:
Authentication session entity representing a single verified login for a todo user.

A session record describes when and where the user authenticated, including connection context (IP, href, referrer) and session expiration, for full auditability. Sessions are subsidiary to a user and always reference their owner. Session expiration is null if the session is still valid. Designed for user self-audit and cross-device management in a privacy-focused todo app.

Used for read-only display to the authenticated user. Modification or deletion operations are controlled elsewhere. Ownership enforced via todo_user_id and API authorization is always by current user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user session. Primary key from todo_user_sessions table.

todo_user_id.description: Reference to the owning user account associated with this session. Foreign key to todo_user.id.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established, for audit logging.

href.description: Connection URL at the moment the session was established. Used for security context and to provide origin details for user self-audit.

referrer.description: Referrer URL when initiating the session. Useful for tracing session origin and context of login.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the session was created. The start time of this login session.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was invalidated. Null if session remains active.
This property is null if the session is still ongoing.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp if the session has ended, or null if still active.

ITodoTodo.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and paginating a user's todo list in the todo_todos table.

Allows clients to request specific pages, apply filters by completion status or creation/completion date, and search by keyword in titles/descriptions. Only operates within scope of authenticated user's own tasks; never allows cross-account data access.

Used in PATCH /todo/user/todos for advanced list view, supporting user privacy and performance.

page.description: The page index for paginated queries (1-based). Default is 1, first page if not specified.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page (page size). Default and max capped at 100.

q.description: Optional search keyword applied to todo titles and descriptions. Case-insensitive, uses partial matching. If blank or null, disables text search.

completed.description: Filter to restrict results to completed (true) or incompleted (false) todos only.

oneOf.description: Earliest creation date from which to include todos. Filter lower bound (inclusive).

created_from.description: Lower-bound filter (inclusive) for todo creation time, or null if not filtering.

oneOf.description: Latest creation date up to which to include todos. Filter upper bound (inclusive).

created_to.description: Upper-bound filter (inclusive) for todo creation time, or null if not filtering.

oneOf.description: Earliest completed_at timestamp for filtering completed todos.

completed_from.description: Lower-bound filter (inclusive) for completed_at timestamp, or null if not filtering.

oneOf.description: Latest completed_at timestamp for filtering completed todos.

completed_to.description: Upper-bound filter (inclusive) for completed_at timestamp, or null if not filtering.

oneOf.description: Field to sort the todo list by. Can sort by creation time, last update, completion, or title.
Field to sort the todo list by. Can sort by creation time, last update, completion, or title.
Field to sort the todo list by. Can sort by creation time, last update, completion, or title.
Field to sort the todo list by. Can sort by creation time, last update, completion, or title.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the todo list by. Can sort by creation time, last update, completion, or title.

oneOf.description: Sort direction (ascending or descending) for the chosen sort_by field.
Sort direction (ascending or descending) for the chosen sort_by field.

sort_order.description: Sort direction (ascending or descending) for the chosen sort_by field.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo task. Primary key of the todo_todos table.

title.description: Short, descriptive title for the todo item. Required and unique per user.

completed.description: Boolean status indicating whether this task is complete.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking when the todo was created. Set automatically on insert.

completed_at.description: Timestamp of completion. Set when the todo is marked as completed, or null if incomplete.

user.description: Summary information for the owning user of this todo.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a todo item in the Todo List application.

Used for displaying task lists or embedding tasks in user contexts. Shows minimal identifying information and completion status, omitting description field and sensitive data. Includes summary of the owning user.

ITodoTodo.description:
A todo task item belonging exclusively to a registered user.

Represents a single actionable item in the user's personal todo list. Each todo item is owned by one user and contains a title (required, unique per user), an optional description, a status flag indicating completion, and related timestamps for creation, updates, and completion.

All relationships, business rules, constraints, and validation requirements as described in the todo_todos Prisma schema are enforced. Ownership is managed via a foreign key to the user. Titles are unique for each user, ensuring no accidental duplicate entries.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each todo item.

title.description: Short, descriptive title for the todo item. Must be unique per user, not blank, maximum 255 characters. Cannot contain only whitespace. Required on creation. Business rules prevent empty or duplicate values.

description.description: Detailed notes or additional context for the todo item. Optional; may be null. Maximum length 1000 characters. Not shown in list displays by default.

completed.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the task is complete. Defaults to false. Can be toggled by user at any time.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the todo was created. Set automatically, immutable after insertion.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to this todo, modified on every edit or status change.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked completed. Set when task is complete, cleared when reverted to incomplete. Null if not completed.

user.description: Reference to the owning user (summary only). Enforces strict single-user data partition and access. Corresponds to todo_user_id property linking this todo to its owner.

ITodoTodo.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new todo entry with minimal required fields, strictly enforcing validation and security rules.

All todos are personal, single-user entries—ownership is assigned automatically based on the authenticated user in the API context and cannot be specified in the request body. The only permitted fields are title (required, unique per user, non-blank) and optional description. No fields exist for completion status or system-managed timestamps in this input type. Security boundaries ensure all operations are confined to the authenticated user's own todo list.

title.description: Required short, descriptive title for the new todo. Cannot be blank, whitespace-only, or duplicate for the same user. Must not exceed 255 characters.

oneOf.description: Additional, optional context or notes. Can be null or omitted on create.
No description provided.

description.description: Optional detailed notes providing additional context for the todo task. Null if omitted. Maximum 1000 characters.

ITodoTodo.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating core fields of an existing todo item. Used as the request body for updating a user's own todo.

Allows changes to the title (required, unique per user, max 255, not blank/whitespace), optional description (up to 1000), and completion state. Ownership, creation timestamp, and user ID cannot be updated. All field and business constraints from the todo_todos schema are enforced.

Fields not in schema are ignored; deletion is not supported by this DTO. Permanent, strictly private, and fully user-owned operation.

title.description: Short, descriptive title for the todo item. Must remain unique per user, not blank, maximum 255 characters. Required for update. Whitespace-only strings are not allowed.

description.description: Detailed notes for the todo item. Optional; can be set, cleared, or truncated. Maximum 1000 characters or may be null.

completed.description: Completion flag. Set true/false to mark as complete/incomplete. Toggling updates the completed_at timestamp automatically.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user. Maps to the primary key in the todo_user table.

email.description: Unique email address for user authentication and account recovery.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the account was created. Immutable.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp marking the account as soft-deleted, used for GDPR and right-to-be-forgotten compliance. Null if active.

ITodoUser.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a registered user account in the Todo app.

Contains unique identification and contact information. Used for display in context of sessions or todo ownership. Does not include password hash or sensitive authentication fields.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user session. Corresponds to the primary key in the todo_user_sessions table.

created_at.description: Time the session was created. Marks session start, set automatically on creation.

expired_at.description: Time when the session expired or was invalidated. Null if session remains active.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established, for audit logging and security context.

href.description: Connection URL at the moment the session was established.

referrer.description: Referrer URL when initiating the session, providing context for session tracking.

user.description: Summary information for the owning user account associated with this session.

ITodoUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for an authentication session for a Todo user account.

Represents a single login/session context for a user, including connection origin and timing metadata. Used to display recent or active sessions and audit activities. Does not include sensitive tokens. Includes summary reference to the owning user account.
